purpose: Connect material property-law changes to affected answer snapshots and place them into a controlled re-verification workflow.

input.change_type: Amendment, commencement, repeal, regulation, judgment, procedure, form/link, source correction or other material change.
input.effective_date: Date the change legally/procedurally takes effect where established.

dependency_resolution.direct_snapshot_matches: Snapshots directly linked to affected canonical objects.
dependency_resolution.indirect_snapshot_matches: Snapshots dependent on changed objects through the dependency graph.
dependency_resolution.historical_snapshot_matches: Historical answers potentially affected only for their relevant legal period.
dependency_resolution.unaffected_snapshots: Snapshots reviewed and determined not materially affected.

reverification_event.reason: Specific legal or procedural dependency that triggered review.

decision_rules: Detected change does not itself establish legal effect.
An answer is not republished solely because a dependency changed.
Effective and commencement dates must be resolved before current-law publication.
Historical snapshots remain preserved even when superseded.
Direct and indirect dependencies must both be considered.
A procedural change can trigger review without changing the underlying entitlement.
A source or link change must not be treated as a substantive legal amendment.
Unresolved legal effect blocks automatic publication.
Material evidence conflicts require explicit review.
No silent stale-answer replacement is permitted.
audit_requirements: Every re-verification event retains its triggering change event.
Every changed answer retains its previous snapshot.
The public answer exposes last-verified status without exposing unnecessary internal identifiers or personal data.
